hypotheses.claim: Global mean-depot-distance normalization plus a generalized savings correction (edge penalty lam, radial asymmetry mu) and a dimensionless capacity-fill reward beta yields a better static merge order than plain Clarke-Wright on dev_24 hetero regimes (tight capacity, eccentric depot, size 100), reaching mean tour length below 16.19 at <2 ms solve time with 100% completion, whereas pairwise (d0i+d0j) normalization destroys far-customer priority and regresses to ~18.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve the vectorized static merge scoring hook around the globally depot-distance-normalized generalized savings family: score(i,j) = [d0i + d0j - lam*dij + mu*|d0i - d0j|]/mean(d0[1:]) + beta*clip((qi+qj)/Q,0,1), searching lam in [1.00,1.20], mu in [0.05,0.18], beta in [0.05,0.20], allowing small bounded extra terms (endpoint demand balance 1-|qi-qj|/(qi+qj), and a mild far-customer retention weight on max(d0i,d0j)) but forbidding any pairwise (d0i+d0j) local normalization; keep a single fully vectorized hook evaluation which ended at ~1.4 ms p50 / 1.5 ms p95 so the 25 ms budget stays ~94% free and no instance degrades to exhausted-incumbent, and push mean dev_24 tour length below the 16.1992 archive incumbent while respecting all feasibility invariants.
